source.paper: unknown US magazine, Advertising Section p. 105 (pulp or popular-science monthly)

summary: A magazine classified section: CLASSIFIED ADVERTISING in heavy condensed old-style caps over a double rule, three columns of justified serif liners divided by hairlines, and centred bold italic category heads between rules. Calm, regular, and very readable.

frame.masthead: Small caps running head 'ADVERTISING SECTION' with folio, then the title in heavy condensed serif caps, double rule beneath.

headers.notes: Bold italic old-style title case, centred, a rule above and below.

units.example: DETECTIVES EARN BIG MONEY. Travel. Excellent opportunity. Experience unnecessary...
units.notes: Opening words in caps (often a complete sentence), body in a sturdy old-style; each ad ends with company, Dept. code and city, and a hairline below.

notes: The copy is a goldmine for a generator: get-rich schemes, patent lawyers, song-poem contests, stammering cures.
Dept. codes (Dept. C-106) are the period equivalent of booking codes.
